 Thursday 1 0 September 2026 Statistical Press Notice NHS referral to treatment (RTT) waiting times data Ju ly 2026 NHS England released statistics today on r eferral to t reatment (RTT) waiting times for consultant - led elective care. The statistics include patients waiting to start treatment at the end of Ju ly 2026 and patients who were treated during Ju ly 2026 . These statistics relate to referral to treatment (RTT) pathways. Some p atients ar e waiting on more than one pathway. Missing d ata for Ju ly 2026 Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (RHQ) , Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust (RA9) and University Hospitals Plymouth (RK9) did not submit any RTT data for Ju ly 2026 . When interpreting RTT data, account should be taken of providers that did not submit data. To aid interpretation, the RTT Overview Timeseries file contains additional key measures at a national level that include estimates for non - reporting acute trusts. E stimates are based on the latest data submitted by non - reporting acute trusts. See Cora Health MSK (NMG, formerly Connect Health Ltd), an independent sector provider, also did not submit RTT data for July 2026. Estimates for non - reporting providers do not routinely include independent sector providers. However, because Cora Health MSK re ports a substantial number of pathways, an estimate has been included in the July 2026 national figures. No estimates have been added retrospectively for missing non - acute NHS providers and independent sector providers in earlier months. We will review the approach before the next publication and, where missing non - acute NHS providers and independent sector p roviders data materially affects national figures, make any necessary revisions to the historical series. Main f indings figures include estimates for missing trusts (see Missing data for July 2026 section) The number of RTT pathways where a patient was waiting to start treatment at the end of Ju ly 2026 was 7. 3 million. Some patients are on multiple pathways. The number of unique patients is estimated to be around 6. 2 million 1 . Among the 7. 3 m illion, in 111,379 cases the patient was waiting more than 52 weeks, in 9,095 cases they were waiting more than 65 weeks, in 1,494 cases they were 1 This is based on analysis of the Waiting List Minimum Data Set (WLMDS), which showed that the ratio of unique NHS numbers to pathways on 2 nd August 2026 was 85:100. The WLMDS extract was taken on 3 rd September 2026, which includes data up to 23 rd August 2026. waiting more than 78 weeks, and in 23 5 cases they were waiting more than 104 weeks. In 65. 4 % of cases the patient had been waiting up to 18 weeks, thus not meeting the 92% standard. During Ju ly 2026 , 1,985,434 new R TT pathway s were started (new RTT period or clock starts). During Ju ly 2026 , 3 28 , 929 pathways were completed as a result of admitted treatment and 1,322,549 were completed in other ways (non - admitted) . For those pathways where the p atient was waiting to start treatment at the end of Ju ly 2026 , the median waiting time was 12 . 0 weeks. The 92 nd percentile waiting time was 38. 4 weeks 2 . Further information Detailed tables of incomplete and completed pathway waiting times by treatment function (specialty), commissioner and provider are available at: http://www.england.nhs.uk/statistics/rtt - waiting - times/ . The commissioner data files include aggregation s of waiting times by sub - ICB, ICB , region and England as a whole. An interactive dashboard of the monthly referral to treatment waiting times statistics is updated as part of the main publication at RTT Dashboard - NHS England Data Dashboard . For April 2021 data onwards, the reporting requirements for the monthly RTT data return were updated further details are available at DCB0095: Consultant - led referral to treatment (RTT) waiting times - NHS Digital ) . The guidance on the recording and reporting of RTT data was updated on 2 February 2024 to say that community service pathways should, from February 2024, no longer be reported in RTT datasets and should instead be captured in community health services data collections change. 2 The median and 92nd percentile figures do not contain estimates for missing trusts (where relevant) . National trends figures include estimates for missing trusts (see Missing data for July 2026 section) Among the 7. 3 million pathways where the patient was waiting to start treatment at the end of Ju ly 2026 , 65. 4 % were waiting up to 18 weeks , an increase of 4. 1 percentage points from the same month in the previous year (chart 1) . The total number of RTT clock starts per working day in the 12 months to Ju ly 2026 was up by 3.0 % compared to the 12 months to Ju ly 2025 ( chart 2). The total number of completed RTT pathways per working day was up by 2. 5 % in the 12 months to Ju ly 2026 compared to the 12 months to Ju ly 2025 ( completed admitted pathways down by 2. 6 % and completed non - admitted pathways up by 3 . 8 %, chart s 3 and 4 ). The number of pathways where the patient was waiting to start treatment (inco m plete pathways) at the end of Ju ly 2026 decreased b y 0.8 % ( 62,027 ) compared to the end of Ju ly 2025 (chart s 5 and 6 ).
